name: Bertolet-Herbein Cabin

dates.note: The survey's physical-history line ('Erected ...') was cut off in the extract, so no date is recorded; the survey's own statement of significance calls it 'a simple and picturesque type of home built by the first settlers in the Pennsylvania-German country' and says its window frames are 'post-Revolutionary'. The survey was prepared August 1960 and said the cabin was then 'in imminent danger of demolition'; its present state and location were not verified here.

refs.note: The survey number as the OCR prints it is 'PA-10^7' in the title and '(HABS No. PA-104?)' in the running heads; both are read as PA-1047, and that is a READING of noisy OCR, marked as one. The location line: 'of Limekiln (Oley Line), Limekiln Vicinity, Berks County, Pennsylvania'.
The item id is the path segment of the data PDF actually fetched; the landing page itself was not opened.

survey.prepared: Prepared by James C. Massey, Architect National Park Service August 1960 (as printed)

quotes.text: This building is one of the few surviving examples of Significance: of a simple and picturesque type of home built "by the first settlers in the Pennsylvania-German country. It is in imminent danger of demolition.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, cover 'Brief Statement of Significance'; the search result's snippet of the same document, no page number

quotes.text: Pronounced Germanic overtones mark this small one-and-a-half story log cabin, and its three-room plan is typical of German building ... ^^Pennsylvania ... Across one end of the house is the kitchen, with entrances at both front and back, and a steep ladder-like stair- way to the attic in an outside corner. 3he larger remainder of the house is divided laterally into two rooms, a sitting room in the front, and behind it, a chamber.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Part I, quoting a published description 'by James C. Massey'; the ellipses are the OCR's own and are quoted as printed; no page marker legible

quotes.text: 1. Over-all dimensions: One-and-a-half stories, rectangular plan, approximately 20 feet by 30 feet.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Part II.B.1; the marker 'Page 4 (HABS No. PA-104?)' follows

quotes.text: 2. Foundations: Rubble, light gray local stone.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Part II.B.2; same span

quotes.text: 3. Wall construction: Log, chinked with mortar.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Part II.B.3; same span

quotes.text: 4. Openings: a. Doorways and doors: Two Dutch half doors, at oppo- site sides of the cabin; crude frames and hardware; three-foot by six-foot stoops at both doors. b. Windows and shutters: Three double-hung windows with broad shutters on original strap hinges. Window frames are post-Revolutionary; six-over-six light windows.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Page 4, Part II.B.4

quotes.text: 5. Roof: a. Shape, covering: Steep gable roof flares at lower third of height—tin covered. Roof construction hand-hewn: no ridge pole, rafters notched into extra large sill set on top of wall. Rafters tied half way up with large wooden pegs. b. Eaves: Overhanging eaves.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Page 4, Part II.B.5

quotes.text: 6. Chimney: Large stone chimney, slightly off-center of the house.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Page 4, Part II.B.6

quotes.text: 1. Floor plans: Rectangular plan; two rooms separated by free-standing fireplace; stairs in corner. Partial cellar.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Page 4, Part II.C.1

quotes.text: 2. Stairway: Simple ladder-like corner stairway without railing—three steps, landing, straight run.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Page 4, Part II.C.2

quotes.text: 4. Wall and ceiling finish: Log and plaster interior finish. Summer beam exposed runs from wall to fire- place and rests on 12-inch by 14-inch chimney beam.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Page 4, Part II.C.4

quotes.text: 9. Heating: Large stone kitchen fireplace, four feet by ten feet, with original wood crane.
quotes.page: HABS No. PA-1047, Part II.C.9; the marker 'Page 5 (HABS No. PA-104?)' follows

measurements.note: Audited 4 Sep 2026 (the Tranche 1 adversarial re-resolution): the survey does not say which figure is the front; the convention across precedents/ is that the FIRST figure printed is overall_width_ft (badin-roque-house reads '27\' x 30\'' the same way), and this record had read the larger. Swapped to the convention; the cabin 'faces southeast'.

note: The Pennsylvania-German channel the node's own prose calls 'the far larger channel', measured by HABS in 1960: a 20 x 30 ft pen with the chimney 'slightly off-center' and a three-room (Massey) or two-room (data page) plan divided by the fireplace -- the survey disagrees with itself on the count and both statements are quoted. The central chimney is the Continental plan the node's own kit distinguishes from the Anglo gable-end pen, so this is the German ancestor and not the Upland South descendant. Seeded 4 Sep 2026.
